summary: Nora can answer a public Instagram summons: somebody listed in identity.toml tags @noraexample in a comment under a post, and she replies once in the comments, or says nothing.
details: Off by default ([social.instagram.summons] enabled = false) and in dry_run by default: the whole turn runs and the reply she would have written is stored in the instagram_summons table, and nothing is posted until mode = "live" and the bridge's own INSTAGRAM_COMMENT_WRITES=on.
Only people in identity.toml, matched by their Instagram igid, can summon her; anyone else is counted and ignored without reading the post or calling the model.

She reads the post and the comments around the summons, with an age on each, and answers with public-only tools (web and X search, reading a post's images by url, the clock, arithmetic). A summons writes no memory, reads no room, and loads a public doctrine with none of the group-chat files.
Each summons is claimed once in Postgres before the model runs, so it is answered at most once; a write whose outcome is unknown is never retried.

The mentions feed is polled every 120 seconds at most (never under 60), one summons reaches the bridge per poll, and the poller backs off up to 30 minutes when the session needs a human or the bridge is reconnecting.
limitations: A summons older than max_age_minutes (60) is recorded stale and never answered, which is also the only brake on a backlog the first time it is enabled.
A summons that is not on the first page of the post's comments is not answered.
Replies over 2,200 characters are refused at the flush and nothing is posted; she is not asked to shorten them.
